headline: Pulleys redirect and multiply force—making the impossible liftable
universal_truth: Complex problems often have simple mechanical solutions
fun_facts: Archimedes reportedly used compound pulleys to single-handedly move a fully-loaded ship
A block and tackle with 4 pulleys lets you lift something with 1/4 the force
Elevators use pulley systems with counterweights to lift heavy loads efficiently
discussion_questions: Where do you see pulleys used today?
Why might redirecting force be as useful as multiplying it?
What other systems use similar principles of mechanical advantage?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Imagine lifting a piano to a third-floor window. Impossible by hand—but with a system of pulleys, one person can do it. Pulleys are simple machines that redirect and multiply force, making the impossible liftable.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: A single pulley changes direction but doesn't multiply force. So how do pulleys become force multipliers? What's the trick that makes a rope and wheel system so powerful?

options.text: Multiple pulleys share the load across several rope sections, dividing the effort needed
options.response: Yes. Each rope segment carries part of the load. Four segments means you pull with 1/4 the force—over 4 times the distance.

options.text: The wheel reduces friction, making everything easier to lift
options.response: Wheels do reduce friction, but the real multiplication comes from rope geometry...

q1.title: Rope Segments
q1.script: In a compound pulley, multiple rope segments support the load. If four segments hold the weight, each carries one-fourth. You pull with one-fourth the force—but pull four times as much rope. Same energy, different arrangement.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Rope Segments"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Direction Matters
q2.script: Even a single pulley helps—not by multiplying force but by redirecting it. Pulling down is easier than pulling up because you add your body weight. Sometimes changing direction is as valuable as multiplying force.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Modern Use
q3.script: Elevators, cranes, and gym equipment all use pulley principles. Elevators add counterweights—so the motor only lifts the difference between car and counterweight. Clever engineering reduces the work needed.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Complex problems often have simple mechanical solutions. Pulleys teach that understanding basic physics unlocks surprising capabilities. Sometimes the right arrangement of simple parts achieves the impossible.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 114. Tomorrow, we'll explore how gears transfer motion. Until then, notice pulleys and pulley-like systems around you—they're more common than you might think.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Pulley Spotting - Find the Simple Solutions
growTrack.learning_objective: Notice mechanical solutions to lifting problems
growTrack.activity: Look for pulley systems today: blinds, flagpoles, construction equipment, gym machines. Each uses the same ancient principle. What heavy things in your life might benefit from mechanical advantage rather than brute force?
